Every AI call of the app goes through one router. The page you are reading always goes first, even while chapters are translated in the background; then chapters and the review, then chat and search, then the home screen. The last 20% of every key's daily quota is kept for translation, so chat and the home screen never use it up. A key set to Automatic uses a light model for chat and extras and its strongest model for the review. A call that fails moves to the next key at once, and a key that keeps failing rests longer each time. Every key also learns how many calls it can run at once: it adds a little after each answer and halves at the first \"too busy\". While you read, if the first key is slow on a page, a second key races it and the first good answer wins. Chapters queued for translation keep going in the background, even after the app is closed.

While you read, the next chapter is translated in the background when the team has at least 3 working keys with quota left. Every model on your phone and all your keys translate each chapter together. What reads the text of each page before it is translated. Both together (the default and the strongest): ML Kit reads fast, PaddleOCR reads every line again on the phone, adds what ML Kit missed (stylised letters, slanted and small text, light text on dark panels, Korean) and replaces ML Kit\'s reading where ML Kit was unsure. PaddleOCR only: the most accurate for hard fonts and Korean. ML Kit only: the fastest and lightest. Lines still unsure after both are read again from their image by a key that sees images. Until PaddleOCR\'s models are on the phone (they download by themselves on Wi-Fi), ML Kit reads alone.

Each part of a chapter now sees what was said on the two pages before it, even while another key is still on them, so who speaks and to whom stays right. Names spelt a little differently from the work\'s glossary are written its way, the reader learns whether a new character is a man or a woman, and your own corrections are found again (they were saved under another key with the Egyptian dialect).

Takes a few minutes; nothing leaves the phone.

For the most speed: turn on the phone\'s performance mode (on RedMagic: the Game Space / turbo slider, or Settings › Battery › Performance), keep it charging and cool (the fan helps), and keep the app\'s battery use on Unrestricted. An app cannot switch the performance mode on by itself.

Automatic: before translating, the app checks the laptop (3 seconds at most, then every minute). It answers: everything goes to it. It does not: the other keys translate, or the phone model when there is no key. Laptop only: nothing else is used. Never the laptop: only the other keys.

To reach the laptop from outside the house: install Tailscale on the laptop and the phone with the same account, and put the name of the laptop here instead of the IP, like http://laptop-name:11434/v1. Without it, the app switches to your other keys or the phone model by itself when you leave.
For an RTX 4060 (8 GB) with 16 GB of RAM. Download the model on the laptop with the command below, then tap Use it. Models bigger than 14B will not fit.

1. Install Ollama from ollama.com.
2. In a terminal: ollama pull aya-expanse:8b
3. Let the phone reach it: set the environment variable OLLAMA_HOST to 0.0.0.0 (Windows: Settings, System, About, Advanced system settings, Environment variables).
4. For speed, add two more: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE = -1 (the model stays loaded, no wait before each chapter) and OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION = 1. Then quit Ollama from the tray and open it again.
5. Allow port 11434 in Windows Firewall for private networks.
6. Find the laptop IP: in a terminal, ipconfig, the IPv4 line (like 192.168.1.50). The address is then http://192.168.1.50:11434/v1
7. Tap Test the connection. The laptop has to stay on and awake while it translates.
Your laptop as a free translation server

In the translation team, Home server: put the address of Ollama on your laptop and it translates for free at home. When it does not answer (out of the house), the other keys or the phone model take over by themselves, and Translating now shows where it runs. Works from outside too with Tailscale.
Fits whole on the RTX 4060: the fastest answers, and among the strongest small models in Arabic. The one to use every day.

Whoever translates (laptop, keys or phone model), a bubble that comes back still in English is translated again so it ends in Arabic, misread words (PAMN for DAMN) are read as meant, sound effects and noise are left as drawn, and a line that was not translated is no longer erased and redrawn in English. Made only to translate: fits on the card, strong in Arabic and quick. It does not scout names or write notes, so use it when speed matters.
How many batches the laptop translates together. 2 suits Ollama as it is. Choose more only after setting the server for it (below): extra calls on a server that runs one at a time only wait.

Ollama (simple): set OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=4 and OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0 in the Windows environment variables, then restart Ollama, and choose 4 above. vLLM (fastest, many calls together): install WSL with Ubuntu, then pip install vllm and run an AWQ 7B model with vllm serve on port 8000; put the laptop address with :8000 above and choose 6 or 8. TabbyAPI (ExLlamaV2, fast on 8 GB): run it with a 4-bit EXL2 model on port 5000 and choose 4. All three speak the same language as the app, nothing else changes.
